findings.evidence: Black point compensation is silently dropped for EVERY gray kTRC source (bpc && kind != Gray). The justification 'a gray kTRC source has black Y = 0 by definition, so BPC is the identity' is false. ICC parametricCurveType types 2-4 can have Y(0) > 0, and Prism's own T0 oracle has ISO 18619 cases against non-zero-black parametric sources (crates/hsk-studio-prism/tests/oracle_t0_analytic.rs:199-200). For such profiles, requested or assumed-on BPC is not applied, yet the loss is filed as PreservedOpaque 'skipped'. The real reason is the open Prism defect PRISM-GRAY-BPC-001, and the module doc (convert.rs:6) claims 'nothing here works around a Prism limit'.
findings.remediation: Skip only when the profile's TRC(0) is 0, else refuse or record a Transformed bpc_unavailable loss until PRISM-GRAY-BPC-001 is fixed

findings.evidence: 16-bit Lab at the default Full65535 scale decodes a/b as raw/65535*255-128 (ICC v4 0x8080 neutral). The test builds its raw values with the same formula ((a+128)*257) and expects the same decode, so it echoes the implementation. If Photoshop stores 16-bit Lab with a 0x8000 neutral, every a/b is biased by -0.498. The assumption is disclosed (lab_channels_assumed_icc_encoding, UNVERIFIED).
findings.remediation: Pin the 16-bit Lab neutral with a Photoshop-authored fixture before claiming the mapping
